chapters.title_en: Who Did Patrick's Homework? & A House, A Home
chapters.title_te: పాట్రిక్ హోంవర్క్ ఎవరు చేశారు? & ఒక ఇల్లు, ఒక నివాసం
chapters.prose_title: Who Did Patrick's Homework? (by Carol Moore)
chapters.poem_title: A House, A Home (by Lorraine M. Halli)
chapters.author: Carol Moore / Lorraine M. Halli
learning_outcomes: Recognize that self-reliance and hard work lead to genuine success.
Distinguish between the physical structure of a 'house' (bricks, stone, wood) and the emotional bonds of a 'home' (family, love, unselfish acts).
Master phrasal verbs, compound words, and rhyming patterns in poetry.
summary_points: Patrick hated homework and loved playing games like baseball and Nintendo.
An elf agreed to grant a wish to do Patrick's homework for 35 days, but constantly asked Patrick for help with dictionary, math tables, and history.
In the process of guiding the elf, Patrick himself studied day and night and scored 'A' grades in all subjects.
The poem distinguishes a house (brick, mortar, glass) from a home (family members caring, sharing, and loving unconditionally).

discourses.prompt: Imagine you are Patrick. Write a diary entry on the day you received straight 'A' grades from your teachers.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What did Patrick think his cat was playing with? What was it really?
According to the poet Lorraine M. Halli, what makes a house a 'home'?

Fill in the blanks with appropriate phrasal verbs from the box: [look up, out of luck, true to his word]. (a) Can you ______ this difficult word in the dictionary? (b) The elf, ______, began to do Patrick's homework.
Write a diary entry as Patrick reflecting on how helping the tiny elf actually transformed you into a model, hardworking student.

chapters.title_en: How the Dog Found Himself a New Master! & The Kite
chapters.title_te: కుక్క తనకు కొత్త యజమానిని ఎలా కనుగొంది! & గాలిపటం
chapters.prose_title: How the Dog Found Himself a New Master! (Folk Tale)
chapters.author: Folk Tale / Harry Behn
learning_outcomes: Trace the evolutionary folk story of dog domestication from wild wolves to man's most loyal companion.
Appreciate the vivid imagery, rhythm, and motion of a flying kite described by Harry Behn.
Learn collective nouns (a pack of wolves, a herd of cows, a flock of sheep) and degrees of comparison.
summary_points: Dogs were once their own masters until one dog decided to serve the strongest creature on earth.
He served the wolf, then the bear, then the lion, but left each upon realizing a stronger master existed.
Finally, seeing the lion afraid of man, the dog chose man as his permanent, faithful companion.
The poem captures the soaring beauty of a bright new kite in the blue sky and its sudden flutter when snagged on a tree.

discourses.prompt: Write a short narrative describing an act of loyalty shown by a pet dog.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did the dog say goodbye to the bear? Who did he choose as his next master?
How does a kite look when it is new in a clear blue sky? When does it become a ragged thing?
Complete each sentence with a suitable collective noun: (a) A ______ of cattle was grazing peacefully in the meadow. (b) A ______ of wolves howled through the cold forest.
Design an attractive poster for the Annual Kite Festival (Sankranti Patang Mahotsav) organized in your town.

chapters.author: Japanese Folktale / Eleanor Farjeon
learning_outcomes: Value filial devotion, obedience, and selflessness towards elderly parents.
Understand how minor sibling quarrels start over petty issues and resolve through mutual realization.
Use suffixes (-ful, -less) and rhyming couplets effectively.
summary_points: Taro, a poor young woodcutter, worked hard to buy expensive sake to warm his frail, shivering old father.
A magical waterfall provided delicious warm sake to Taro because of his noble devotion, but yielded only plain cold water to greedy villagers.
The Emperor of Japan rewarded Taro with twenty pieces of gold to encourage all children to honor and obey their parents.
The poem portrays brother-sister quarreling: beginning from a minor thing, turning bitter, and ending with a warm apology.

discourses.prompt: Write a letter to your friend describing why Taro's filial devotion inspired you.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did the magic waterfall give Taro sake and other people only cold water?
How did the quarrel between the siblings in Eleanor Farjeon's poem start and how did it end?
Make nouns from the following adjectives by adding '-ness' or '-ity': (a) honest, (b) kind, (c) noble, (d) bitter.
Write a formal letter to your school Principal requesting permission to stage a play on 'Taro's Reward' for Parents' Day.

chapters.title_en: An Indian – American Woman in Space: Kalpana Chawla & Beauty
chapters.title_te: అంతరిక్షంలో ఒక భారతీయ - అమెరికన్ మహిళ: కల్పనా చావ్లా & అందం
chapters.prose_title: An Indian – American Woman in Space: Kalpana Chawla (Biographical Prose)
chapters.author: Biographical Feature / E-Yeh-Shure
learning_outcomes: Get inspired by Kalpana Chawla's grit, determination, and historic aerospace achievements.
Understand that true beauty exists not only in external sights and sounds, but within good deeds and honest thoughts.
Form technical vocabulary related to space exploration and prefixes (un-, in-, dis-).
summary_points: Kalpana Chawla, born in Karnal (Haryana), graduated in aeronautical engineering and became the first Indian-born woman astronaut in space.
She flew her first mission on Columbia in 1997 and spent 16 days in space doing 80 scientific experiments.
Tragically, Space Shuttle Columbia disintegrated on February 1, 2003 during atmospheric re-entry, claiming the lives of all seven crew members.
E-Yeh-Shure's poem reveals beauty is seen in sunlight, corn, and trees; heard in wind, rain, and singing; and felt inside one's own mind in noble deeds.

discourses.prompt: Write a biographical tribute on Kalpana Chawla highlighting her inspirational message to youth: 'The path from dreams to success does exist'.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was Kalpana Chawla's inspirational message to students of Punjab Engineering College from aboard Columbia?
According to the poet E-Yeh-Shure, where can beauty be seen, heard, and experienced within oneself?
Add suitable prefixes (un-, in-, dis-) to create antonyms: (a) dependent, (b) regular, (c) approve, (d) conscious.
Imagine you were invited to give a morning assembly speech on 'National Science Day'. Prepare a speech honoring the scientific spirit of Kalpana Chawla.

chapters.title_en: A Different Kind of School & Where Do All the Teachers Go?
chapters.title_te: ఒక విభిన్నమైన పాఠశాల & ఉపాధ్యాయులందరూ ఎక్కడికి వెళతారు?
chapters.prose_title: A Different Kind of School (by E.V. Lucas)
chapters.poem_title: Where Do All the Teachers Go? (by Peter Dixon)
chapters.author: E.V. Lucas / Peter Dixon
learning_outcomes: Cultivate deep empathy, sensitivity, and helpfulness towards differently-abled persons.
Appreciate experimental schooling where character, compassion, and shared responsibility are taught as living experiences.
Understand modal auxiliaries (can, could, should, must) and child perceptions of teachers.
summary_points: Miss Beam's school focused on teaching kindness, citizenship, and thoughtfulness rather than just rote scholastic knowledge.
Students observed simulated days: Blind Day, Lame Day, Deaf Day, Injured Day, and Dumb Day to experience disabilities first-hand.
On Blind Day, eyes were bandaged overnight and a classmate acted as helper, creating mutual compassion.
Peter Dixon's poem humorously explores a six-year-old child's curiosity about whether teachers live ordinary human lives (washing socks, wearing pajamas, watching TV).

discourses.prompt: Draft a notice informing students about an upcoming 'Sensitivity and Inclusion Week' organized at your school.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was the main system and aim of Miss Beam's school according to the author?
Which day did the children find the most difficult in Miss Beam's school? Why?
Fill in blanks with appropriate modals (should, must, can): (a) We ______ be kind and sensitive to disabled people. (b) ______ you guide me across the busy street?
Draft a notice for your school notice board inviting volunteers to assist visually impaired students during their annual exams.

chapters.title_en: Who I Am & The Wonderful Words
chapters.prose_title: Who I Am (Many Voices: Radha, Nasir, Rohit, Serbjit, Peter, Dolma)
chapters.author: NCERT Voices / Mary O'Neill
learning_outcomes: Celebrate diversity in human personalities, aspirations, talents, and multiple intelligences.
Recognize that every individual has unique strengths (visual, bodily-kinesthetic, interpersonal, musical).
Understand the creative power of words to express thoughts clearly and beautifully.
summary_points: Six children voice their dreams: Radha loves climbing trees; Nasir wants to become a seed collector to save family cotton crops; Rohit dreams of world travel; Serbjit gets angry when adults disbelieve truth; Peter loves cinema Sundays; Dolma aspires to become Prime Minister of India.
The lesson demonstrates multiple intelligences theory: visual, musical, bodily, interpersonal, and mathematical.
Mary O'Neill's poem reminds us never to let a thought shrivel and die for lack of words; English is a wonderful game to groom and pair thoughts.

figures_of_speech: metaphor: Words are the food and dress of thought

discourses.prompt: Write a self-profile essay entitled 'Who I Am: My Strengths, Hobbies, and Aspirations'.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why does Nasir want to learn how to preserve seeds? How will it help his family?
Why does the poet Mary O'Neill say that 'words are the food and dress of thought'?

Match the personality types with their descriptions: (a) Bodily-Kinesthetic, (b) Interpersonal. Descriptions: (1) Good at understanding people and feelings, (2) Good with body movement, sports, and crafts.
Write a descriptive essay on 'My Life Goal: What I Want to Become and How I Plan to Serve Society'.

chapters.author: Munshi Premchand / Rabindranath Tagore
learning_outcomes: Understand that justice transcends personal friendship ('The voice of the Panch is the voice of God').
Analyze character development and reconciliation between Jumman Shaikh and Algu Chowdhry.
Appreciate Rabindranath Tagore's depiction of a child's yearning for carefree freedom when observing hawkers, gardeners, and night watchmen.
summary_points: Jumman Shaikh and Algu Chowdhry were intimate village friends.
When Jumman's aged aunt transferred her property, Jumman and his wife mistreated her; the aunt took her grievance to the village panchayat.
Algu, chosen as head Panch, gave a verdict against Jumman, causing enmity.
Later, when Algu's own bullock dispute reached the Panchayat, Jumman was made head Panch and realized the solemn duty of impartiality, ruling in Algu's favor.
In 'Vocation', a schoolboy wishes to become a bangle-seller, a gardener, or a night watchman walking with a lantern, envying their apparent freedom.

compound_sentences: coordinating conjunctions: and, but, yet, so

discourses.prompt: Write a conversation between Algu Chowdhry and Jumman Shaikh after the panchayat verdict when they reconcile as true friends.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What did the aunt mean when she said: 'The Panch knows neither friend nor enemy'? How was this proved in the story?
Why does the child in Rabindranath Tagore's poem 'Vocation' wish to become a gardener?
Use the following idiomatic phrases in meaningful sentences of your own: (a) take to heart, (b) make up one's mind.
Write a narrative story illustrating the proverb: 'Truth and justice always triumph in the end'.

chapters.author: Ruskin Bond
learning_outcomes: Appreciate nature, giant banyan trees as flourishing ecosystems, and keen wildlife observation.
Analyze Ruskin Bond's vivid narrative style describing the classic wilderness combat between a grey mongoose and a black cobra.
Understand sensory descriptive language, motion verbs, and adjectives of drama.
summary_points: The author as a boy spent hours reading in the branches of a grand sixty-year-old banyan tree.
From his hidden platform on a warm April afternoon, he witnessed a thrilling duel between a three-foot mongoose and a six-foot black cobra.
A crow and a myna watched the fight, trying to join the fray; the crow was struck by the cobra and died, while the myna stayed on a safe cactus.
With lightning speed and tactical dodging, the mongoose wore out the venomous cobra and ultimately emerged victorious.

discourses.prompt: Write an eyewitness account of the dramatic battle between the mongoose and cobra observed from the banyan tree.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the warning signs and battle tactics used by the cobra to terrify the mongoose?
What happened to the crow when it repeatedly tried to interfere in the fight between the snake and mongoose?
Identify the adverbs in the following sentences and state their type: (a) The mongoose darted swiftly into the bushes. (b) The cobra defended itself cautiously.
Write a descriptive article for your school magazine entitled 'The Grand Old Banyan Tree: A Miniature Wildlife Sanctuary'.
